text: Lakebase is a fully managed, serverless Postgres database built directly into the Databricks Data + AI Platform. The key phrase is built into the platform, not connected to it — it makes lakehouse data directly available to real-time applications and AI agents without a hand-built reverse-ETL pipeline in between.

Before Lakebase, serving curated lakehouse data to an operational application meant provisioning a separate OLTP database, building a custom reverse-ETL pipeline, and keeping that pipeline running correctly forever. That's real, recurring engineering work whose entire purpose is just moving data that's already correct from one place to another. Lakebase collapses it — sync is built in.

This is the single most practical fact in this lesson, and it's a genuine trade-off, not a detail. A continuous sync pipeline, configured with a declared primary key, runs 10 to 15 seconds behind — simple, Databricks manages it. The ForeachWriter pattern gets you 200 to 300 milliseconds instead, at the cost of managing your own streaming query and checkpoint. Pick continuous sync for an ordinary dashboard, ForeachWriter for fraud scoring or a live map.

Databricks' own published example, a food-delivery company called Data Diners: a driver's phone emits GPS telemetry through the Zerobus SDK straight into Delta. A continuous sync pipeline pushes updated records into Lakebase. A FastAPI backend streams updates over WebSockets. And a Databricks Apps front end visualizes it live for dispatchers. Zerobus solved the ingestion hop, Lakebase solves serving it back out — neither needed a message bus or hand-built reverse ETL anywhere in the chain.
